name: The window does one task
sees: The product's own window, large and held on screen, does the one thing the page promises the visitor (the invoice sent, the booking made, the report shared), and every beat changes about a third of the window: the list answers with a full-size row that takes the accent, the panel that does the work opens over the whole list, the action is pressed and the panel closes on the result, the figure that proves it rolls at display size in a band that takes the accent. The task is the promise kept, in the product's real labels and figures, never a tour of the interface for its own sake. The section's heading states that promise; the window proves it.
beats: the request types into the field as the new row pushes in at the top of the list, over the visitor's rows already there, and takes the accent fill → the panel that does the work opens over the whole list, edge to edge (the draft, its lines, its total at display size, its action) → the action is pressed and the panel closes on the result (the row's status changes) → the figure that proves it rolls at display size in a band across the window's foot, and the band takes the accent fill as the row lets it go; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop with its heading in view, the window nearly the full width: the field, three short columns of the list, the panel opening over all of it, the same four beats.

name: The agent works beside its result
sees: One line of request, the agent's own status line under it, and the rows it works on at full size, held on screen while it works. The rows are in the window from its first state, the visitor's own entries before the agent touches them: the agent finds and changes them, it never brings them into an empty table. The request is the job the page promises to take off the visitor's hands; each status names what the agent does to the rows in view, the rows it acts on take the accent fill while it works on them (whole rows, so each beat changes about a third of the window), and it ends on the result the visitor wanted at display size, in the accent (the mistake found, the reply drafted, the books balanced), never on a bare "Done".
beats: the request types in, the agent's status line takes the accent as a band across the window and every row it reads takes the accent fill: "Reading 412 entries" → "Checking against the bank feed": the fill leaves the rows that are in order and stays on the two it found → "Fixed: a duplicate refund" as the fill leaves them, the wrong figure rolls to the right one and the total, at display size in a band across the window's foot, rolls and the band takes the accent; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop with its heading in view: the request and the status band over the rows, three short columns, nearly the full width.

name: The order travels the board
sees: A board of the visitor's own items in three columns of type, held on screen while one item travels it: the counts at display size, the items as lines of type set apart by space, never cards or column boxes, the columns filled to the same depth. The item that moves is the one the promise is about and the only one filled (the accent, its contents shown while it works), never one card among look-alikes; as it arrives and travels the items round it make room, so each beat moves about a third of the window; the column it reaches is the result the visitor wants (an order shipped the day it lands, a ticket closed before lunch). Only for a product whose promise is a move from one state to the next (orders, tickets, deals, bookings, candidates): for notes, documents or anything that is not a pipeline this replay is the wrong one (draw.mjs --redraw replay).
beats: the new item pushes in at the top of the first column, filled with the accent and its contents shown, the count above it rolling at display size → it travels to the next column at full size while the items there make room and both counts change → it reaches the column that means the promise kept, its line changes to the result ("Shipped 16:40") and that column's count rolls at display size in the accent; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop with its heading in view: the three columns stacked, two items each, the item travelling down between them at full width.

name: Teammates take turns
sees: One shared object (a plan, a document, a design) and two or three people, each making one large change in turn, held on screen while they work. Each change is a whole block (a step moved, a figure filled with its breakdown, a comment opened beside a step), filled with the accent while it changes and carrying its author's name inside it, so each turn changes about a third of the window; never a cursor gliding about or a name tag flying over the page. The object ends agreed, which is what the page promises a team (the plan agreed without a meeting, the review done in a day), and that state is the decisive change, large and in the accent.
beats: "Ines" moves a whole step two places down, the step filled with the accent and her name in it → the agent fills the missing figure and its breakdown, the block filled and named → "Tom" opens a comment on the ink beside a step and its deadline lands in the step → the comment closes as the object's head, a band across the window's top, changes to agreed at the heading size and takes the accent fill; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop with its heading in view: the object's blocks one under another, the names inside them, nearly the full width.

name: Edit the source, the output rebuilds
sees: The source (a query, a formula, a config) over the output it makes, held on screen while one value changes. The page's promise is that one edit is enough, so the output is the large part of the window (a chart across it, a table, a rendered page) and it re-forms in front of the visitor: the answer they were after, rebuilt. Each beat changes about a third of the window, and the read-out that proves it ends large and in the accent.
beats: the value in the source takes the accent and its menu of choices opens over a third of the output, on the ink or the accent → the choice is made, the menu closes and the output re-forms (the same marks travel to new places and new ones grow in: four bars become thirteen) → the read-out at display size, in a band across the window's foot, re-counts ("1,240 → 3,912 orders") and the band takes the accent fill; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop with its heading in view: the source line over the output, stacked, nearly the full width.

name: The view moves in on the live screen
sees: The whole screen of the product with three feature lines beside it, held on screen while the view moves in on one region after another like a camera: at each stop the region fills the window at nearly twice its size, a value changes there and takes the accent, and the matching line turns to full ink. Each stop is one thing the product does for the visitor (counts the stock, reorders what runs low, keeps the total right); the last stop moves back out to the whole screen, where the total that proves it takes the accent at display size. The lines stand beside the window, so neither column is left empty.
beats: the view moves in on region one and its row takes the accent as the value rolls (38 → 41) → it moves across to region two, where a status changes (Low → Ordered, 500) → it moves back out to the whole screen as the total recalculates at display size and takes the accent; the matching feature line beside the window turns full ink at each stop, and the lines are buttons that scroll to their stop; each stop about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop with its heading in view: the three lines in a row above the window, nearly the full width. The rows are full width there, so the view does not move in: at each stop the row takes the accent and its value changes.
